clue.text: Spoil male embraced by frivolous sweet thing

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it

indicators.note: being embraced by something means sitting inside it, so the letter for male goes within the word for frivolous

parts.note: shallow means lacking depth, frivolous

explanation.surface: Someone shallow and frivolous ruins a man by smothering him with sweetness.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft spongy confection is a classic example of a sweet treat.

clue.text: Sailor on leave engaging adult to get acquainted

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed on top of, so the sailor comes first

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the word for leave holds the letter

parts.note: rest is time off, a break or leave
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

explanation.surface: A sailor on shore leave meets a grown-up to get to know them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link; 'keep abreast of' means stay informed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abreast of something is to be up to date with it, informed and familiar.

clue.text: Show's act peels, dancing around clubs

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the abbreviation
dancing shows the letters moving about into a new order

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A performance in which an act strips off while dancing around nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges ACT PEELS to SPETACLE, and 'around' sets C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive public display or show.

clue.text: Marks by the compiler's editor made a charade

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for marks, the old German currency
the compiler's means 'the compiler is', from the setter's view I'M

explanation.surface: Annotations by the setter's editor turned something into a mere pretence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins pieces. 'the compiler's' expands to 'I am', the setter speaking of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game charades players act out words silently, so to perform one is to act without speaking.

clue.text: Reasonable, getting grip oddly in pub

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for pub

parts.note: the local is one's neighbourhood pub in Britain

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and other odd-placed letters of the word

explanation.surface: Getting a firm hold, strangely, while drinking in a pub seems sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link. 'oddly' takes G and I from grip; THE LOCAL is British for your nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical means following sound reasoning, so sensible or rational.

clue.text: Stormed taking part in undercover ransom

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A storming squad takes part in a covert ransom operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun a position is to storm and take it by force.

clue.text: Sympathise with company partner employing tight person

indicators.note: employing means using within, so the word for partner holds the other piece

parts.note: a mate is a partner
a miser is someone tight with money

explanation.surface: Feeling for a firm whose partner hires a stingy employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To commiserate is to express pity or sympathy for someone's misfortune.

clue.text: Seeing that rehearsal missing one of the stars

parts.note: as can mean since or seeing that

indicators.note: missing means the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a trial run is a practice, a rehearsal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rehearsal lacks one of its star performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of the stars' looks like a cast member, but 'one' is I and 'of the stars' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral means relating to or coming from the stars, celestial.

clue.text: Old bishop accompanying minister to see

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
to minister to people is to serve them

explanation.surface: An elderly bishop goes along with a cleric to visit someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks like a noun for a cleric but works as the verb 'to attend to'; 'accompanying' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something is to notice or watch it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Draw French painter framing first of gouaches

indicators.note: framing means surrounding, so the painter's name goes round the letter taken

parts.note: Édouard Manet was a French Impressionist-era painter

indicators.note: first of means take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An artist sketches with a French master's gouache paintings around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb about sketching, but here it is a noun: an attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that pulls people in is an attraction, and a magnet is a figurative attraction.

clue.text: Wasting spare time on ape

indicators.note: wasting means squandering, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Frittering away free time on monkeying about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ape' looks like the animal but it is the verb to mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy or mimic them, as an impersonator does.

clue.text: Waspish matron bustling about end of ward

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the extra letter
bustling suggests busy disordered movement, so the letters of the word are rearranged
end of means take only the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued hospital matron bustles around the end of the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bustling' rearranges MATRON to MORANT, and 'about' puts that round D, the last letter of ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit is biting and caustic, so it shares the stinging sense of waspish.

clue.text: Endless lure shown by strange modesty

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a decoy is a lure used to entice
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An unending temptation is revealed through some odd sense of propriety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims DECOY to DECO. RUM meaning strange is old-fashioned British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, seemly behaviour, overlapping with modesty and propriety.

clue.text: Crack opening round side of pants

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the opening word goes round the letter

parts.note: a slit is a narrow opening

indicators.note: side of here means the leading edge, the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tear appears around the side of someone's trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A split is a crack or fissure, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Church and State split by new problem

indicators.note: split by means the word is broken open with another letter inside

parts.note: to state is to allege, assert

explanation.surface: Church and State divided by a fresh issue sounds like a constitutional crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun, the nation, but it is the verb 'to declare'.
explanation.definitionFit: A challenge is a demanding task or difficulty, so a problem in the broad sense.

clue.text: Best cafe trattoria boxing up handmade products

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards
boxing means holding inside, so the answer is a letter run within these words

explanation.surface: The finest café and trattoria are packing away handcrafted goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' takes STCAFETRA from inside 'Best cafe trattoria', and 'up' reads it in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Artefacts are objects made by humans, such as tools or crafts.

clue.text: Begrudge suppressing endless desire rising again

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down within, so the word for begrudge contains the other piece

parts.note: to begrudge something is to resent it

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: Resenting someone while holding back a constant longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final letter of the word for desire before 'suppressing' places it inside; 'rising again' is an adjective, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent describes something reviving, coming back up after a decline.

clue.text: Small, more sinuous snake

parts.note: lither is the comparative of lithe, supple, sinuous

explanation.surface: A small, extra-supple serpent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snake' is the verb to move like a snake, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To slither is to slide along with a sinuous, sideways motion like a serpent.

clue.text: Swimming round catching fish

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the round shape encloses the fish

parts.note: a ring is a round shape
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Going in circles while trying to land a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' looks aquatic but means dizzy, as when a head swims.
explanation.definitionFit: When the head swims one feels giddy and dizzy, staggering.

clue.text: Heads of titled old families for starters

definitions.text: Heads of titled old families for starters

indicators.note: heads of means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The chief members of aristocratic old families, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'titled old families for starters' spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes such people.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffs is British slang for upper-class, wealthy people, such as the heads of aristocratic families.

clue.text: Missile flew containing power discharge

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the word for flew wraps the letter

parts.note: tore can mean rushed or flew along
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
to discharge a duty is to do it

explanation.surface: A rocket sped off, holding enough energy for a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' looks like firing the missile, but means carry out, as in discharging one's duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater explosive weapon is a type of guided missile.

clue.text: Frozen fingertip's stiff

parts.note: the tip of the word finger is its first letter
rigid means stiff, unbending

explanation.surface: A fingertip frozen stiff with cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means very cold, icy, as frozen things are.

clue.text: Muscles shake ends of pectorals

parts.note: a trice is an instant, as is a shake in 'in two shakes'

indicators.note: ends of means take the outer letters, first and last, of the next word

explanation.surface: Gym talk: flexing the arms while the edges of the chest muscles quiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shake' looks like a verb but is the noun for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large muscle at the back of the upper arm; the word is both singular and plural.

clue.text: Tones rising maybe, caught in traffic

indicators.note: in means placed within the word for trade

parts.note: traffic as trade or dealing gives a sale
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Musical notes climbing, perhaps, heard while stuck in traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like cars but means trade; 'maybe' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical scale is a series of notes ascending or descending, of which a rising run is an example.

clue.text: Strange France initially overturned monarchy

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: a reign is a monarch's rule, monarchy in action

explanation.surface: France famously toppled its kings in the Revolution, which seems strange to royalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' looks like a reversal signal, but it only lends its first letter, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign can mean alien or unfamiliar, hence odd and unknown.

clue.text: Victoria, perhaps, in Australia?

parts.note: Victoria seems to be the Australian state, but it is a woman's name, and Australian slang has a word for a woman

explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is an Australian state, which is the false trail; read it as a girl's name and the slang term for a young woman Down Under follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a girl or woman, of whom someone named Victoria is an example.

clue.text: Cold? The man with spray is needed!

definitions.text: Cold? The man with spray is needed!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
he is the pronoun for a man
a mist is a fine spray

explanation.surface: Got a cold? Then you need the pharmacist with a nasal spray.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: in Britain the chemist is the pharmacy you visit for cold remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the pharmacist or pharmacy shop, where cold sprays are sold.

clue.text: Forward motion seeing prisoners go free

indicators.note: setting the letters free lets them break out of order and rearrange

explanation.surface: Letting inmates go free is seen as a step forward in penal reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Progression is movement onward or advance, a forward development.
